description: Deposition-vs-reuse cue lexicon for classifying data-citation mentions as Primary/Secondary from sentence context. Applied to the sentence containing the accession/DOI. RE2-compatible, case-insensitive via (?i). Scoring: sum weights (primary positive, secondary negative) over all of a pair's mention sentences; classify Primary if score >= +2, Secondary if <= -2, else unresolved -> LLM cascade. Location modifiers applied separately.

primary_cues.note: standard DAS phrasing: 'The datasets generated ... are available'
usually repository submission when co-mentioned with an accession
own-data DAS phrasing; weaker because reuse statements also use it
'under accession number X' — weak alone, both directions use it

secondary_cues.pattern: (?i)\bfrom (the )?(NCBI|GenBank|GEO|SRA|ENA|DDBJ|PDB|UniProt|Ensembl|ArrayExpress|Gene Expression Omnibus|Protein Data Bank|Sequence Read Archive)\b

secondary_cues.note: access-date phrasing marks retrieval of existing data

location_modifiers.note: a data-availability statement in the generating paper overwhelmingly describes its own deposits
an ID that only resolves via a bibliography entry points at someone else's deposit

notes: RE2 has no lookbehind/lookahead; all patterns are plain alternation/quantifier regexes.
Cues score the SENTENCE, aggregated per (publication_id, dataset_id) by summing across all mention sentences, then optionally smoothed per (publication_id, family) by majority.
Thresholds (+2/-2) chosen so a single strong cue OR two medium cues resolve a pair; tune against the gold set.

Known tensions: 'made available under' appears in both own-deposit DAS and reuse statements (kept weak); 'previously deposited' is Secondary despite containing 'deposited' — the secondary cue outweighs it only via prev_published, so sentences with both score ~0 and fall through to the LLM, which is the right failure mode.
